entries.grounds: Mutant drops RecursionError from the same `except (OSError, ValueError, RecursionError)` at :517. json.loads raises RecursionError only on very deep nesting: measured on this interpreter (python3 -P -B), `json.loads('['*n+']'*n)` parses at n=32820/50000/100000 and first raises RecursionError near n=200000 (~400000 bytes). So the dropped branch is unreachable for any realistic request; it defends only an adversarial worker emitting ~400 KB of nested brackets on a multi-thousand-file request. ValueError stays. entries.grounds: file_artifact.py:431-433 validates the worker's skipped_binary: `if not isinstance(skipped, list) or not all(index(i) for i in skipped) or skipped != sorted(set(skipped)): bad('skipped_binary is not an ascending list of file indexes')`. The contract is that skipped_binary is a strictly ascending, de-duplicated list of file indexes (the real GREP_WORKER :382-408 appends indexes as it iterates, so it emits them ascending). The mutant replaces `sorted(set(skipped))` with `list(set(skipped))`, i.e. it compares against CPython set-iteration order instead of ascending order. Measured on this interpreter (python3 -P -B): `list(set([2,1]))`==[1,2]==`sorted(set([2,1]))`, which is why the existing 'skipped out of order' case {skipped_binary:[2,1]} (test_v21_fa_grep_worker.py:680) does NOT distinguish the two and the mutant survives. But `list(set([7,8]))`==[8,7] while `sorted(set([7,8]))`==[7,8]: so the mutant (a) WRONGLY ACCEPTS a non-ascending result skipped_binary=[8,7] (original rejects it as BAD_RESULT) and, worse, (b) WRONGLY REJECTS a VALID ascending result skipped_binary=[7,8] (original accepts it) — a real repository with binary (NUL) files at indexes 7 and 8 and >=9 files sent yields the ascending [7,8] from the real worker, which the mutant turns into a BAD_RESULT -> HARNESS_FAILED. A reader depends on the ascending-order check: a test is owed. Ran tests.v2.test_v21_fa_grep_worker on the mutant: PASS (survives) — the gap is real, the kill is missing.

entries.refutation: Input: call fa._worker_facts({'files':9,'matches':0,'skipped_binary':[7,8],'locations':[]}, rels) with rels of length 9 (e.g. ['f0.py',...,'f8.py']). Reader: _worker_facts' contract that a valid ascending skipped_binary is accepted and named (file_artifact.py:431-434,438,449) — and conversely that a non-ascending one is BAD_RESULT. Sketch: assert the ORIGINAL returns {'present':True, ..., 'skipped_binary':['f7.py','f8.py'], ...} (a normal multi-binary-file result accepted) AND that skipped_binary=[8,7] raises WorkerFailed('BAD_RESULT') with 'skipped_binary is not an ascending list of file indexes'. The existing suite only uses skipped_binary of length 0/1 in good cases and [2,1] in the bad case (all of which set-iterate ascending), so none exercises an index pair whose set-iteration order differs from sorted; [7,8]/[8,7] does. This test FAILS on the mutant (it refuses the valid [7,8], or accepts the invalid [8,7]) and PASSES unmutated -> kills index 56.
